title: CYBERSECURITY OF MARKET RETAILERS AGAINST COORDINATED ATTACKS IN DEREGULATED ELECTRICITY MARKETS
abstract: This thesis presents the development and evaluation of a hybrid framework integrating Digital Twins (DT) and Machine Learning (ML) for anomaly detection within electricity markets. The framework is designed to differentiate between isolated anomalies, disturbances targeting individual retailers, and coordinated attacks, which involve simultaneous disruptions across multiple market participants. Initially developed using a case study of the PJM electricity market, the framework’s real-world applicability was further validated through an analysis of Electric Vehicle (EV) charging systems within the NYISO electricity market.

title: Assessing the strength of machine learning and deep learning models for network anomaly detection: insights from multi-dataset cybersecurity analysis
abstract: Abstract Network anomaly detection is one of the key aspects to be considered for the protection of modern digital infrastructures against changing cyber-attacks. As networks are becoming increasingly larger and complex, the processing of millions of flows in real time is a high-performance computing (HPC) issue that requires parallel and distributed computing. This paper aims to evaluate the performance of six anomaly detection models: four machine learning models (Random Forest, Isolation Forest, Local Outlier Factor, One-Class SVM) and two deep learning models (LSTM-CNN, Autoencoder). The performance evaluation is done using four public datasets (UNSW-NB15, CICIDS-2017, NSL-KDD, ToN-IoT) with over five million data records. The results showed that parallel preprocessing achieves a 10.8 times speedup on 16 CPU cores, while GPU achieves a 35 times speedup for deep learning models. Among the models, the performance of the Random Forest is found to be stable with F1 > 0.95.

title: Autonomous Penetration Analyst 3.0: A Safety-Gated Framework for Offline Lab Vulnerability Validation
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This work presents Autonomous Penetration Analyst 3.0, a safety-gated framework designed for offline laboratory vulnerability validation and controlled cybersecurity experimentation. The framework focuses on enabling autonomous or semi-autonomous penetration analysis within isolated environments while enforcing operational safety boundaries to reduce misuse risks. The proposed architecture integrates automated reconnaissance, vulnerability assessment workflows, controlled exploit validation, and safety-governed execution policies. Unlike unrestricted offensive automation systems, the framework emphasizes offline laboratory deployment, sandboxed execution, and restricted target validation to support ethical cybersecurity research and defensive testing practices. The study explores how autonomous security analysis pipelines can improve repeatability, efficiency, and structured reporting in research-oriented penetration testing environments. Additional attention is given to safety gating mechanisms, execution constraints, auditability, and operational transparency to ensure controlled experimentation. This research is intended for academic study, defensive cybersecurity research, and authorized laboratory testing only. The framework is not designed for unauthorized access, offensive deployment, or real-world malicious operations. Keywords: cybersecurity, autonomous penetration testing, vulnerability validation, offline lab security, AI-assisted security analysis, defensive research, ethical hacking, safety-gated systems

title: Requirements to Safety, Security, and Designing of SMR Digital Infrastructure
abstract: Small modular reactor (SMR) projects in the United States, Canada, and several European countries demonstrate a growing trend toward developing SMRs as high-tech critical energy infrastructure. Despite their expected benefits, these projects introduce new challenges for digital infrastructure (DI) developers, operating organizations, and regulatory authorities, particularly related to safety, cybersecurity, and the functional safety of instrumentation and control systems (I&C). SMR projects have specific characteristics related to location, design, construction, operation, maintenance, licensing, and communication that must be considered when implementing digital technologies. These features create new requirements for DI and I&C systems and require careful consideration of potential safety and cybersecurity risks. This chapter analyzes the characteristics of SMR projects and their impact on digital infrastructure and I&C systems. This classify SMR features from the perspective of DI safety and cybersecurity and highlight their importance for DI specification and risk management.

title: Cyber Guardian: A Complete Security Toolkit for Android
authors: Gaddam Jayasimha Reddy; Rishi Kumar Yadav; Shivam Kashinath Bablikar; Vivek Mahesh Shinde; Tushar B . Khaloge
venue: International Scientific Journal of Engineering and Management
abstract: The proliferation of mobile devices and internet-based services has significantly increased user exposure to cyber threats such as malware infections, phishing attacks, and data breaches. This paper presents Cyber Guardian — a comprehensive, integrated Android security toolkit developed using Kotlin. The application combines three core modules: a Malware Scanner, a Phishing Link Detector, and a Cybersecurity Awareness Program. The malware scanner employs rule-based and regex-driven pattern analysis along with risky permission detection to identify potentially harmful applications. The phishing module integrates the VirusTotal API for real-time URL threat analysis across multiple antivirus engines. The awareness module delivers structured educational content to improve user knowledge of safe digital practices. Testing results confirm reliable threat detection, real-time phishing classification, and effective awareness delivery, making Cyber Guardian a practical solution for everyday mobile cybersecurity challenges.Keywords — Cybersecurity; Malware Detection; Phishing Detection; Kotlin; Android Security; VirusTotal API; Mobile Application; URL Analysis; Threat Detection; User Awareness

title: EXSS: an Educational Emulator for Cross-Site Scripting Attacks
authors: Bianca Guarizi; Isabela Alves; Júlia Fernandez e Souza; Guilherme Pimentel; João André Watanabe; Dalbert Mascarenhas; Ian Bastos; Marcelo Rubinstein; Igor De MOraes
venue: Journal of the Brazilian Computer Society
abstract: This article proposes a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attack emulator for learning in cybersecurity. The emulator allows users to identify a website vulnerable to XSS attacks in a controlled environment. The identification of vulnerabilities is achieved through activities that consist of a theoretical introduction to the topic, followed by practical procedures for conducting XSS vulnerability tests on a Web server running on a virtual machine. Activities are developed for different levels of knowledge. The particularity of the proposed emulator is its educational approach and its goal is to raise awareness among undergraduate students and professionals to develop less vulnerable websites.

title: Phiraxon AI: A Hybrid Defensive Phishing Analysis Prototype with Rule-Based Detection, Static Attachment Inspection, IOC Extraction and Machine Learning
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Phiraxon AI is a defensive cybersecurity prototype for analyzing suspicious emails, URLs, raw email headers and uploaded attachments. The system combines rule-based phishing indicators, URL structure analysis, email header spoofing checks, static attachment inspection, indicator-of-compromise extraction and a lightweight machine learning phishing classifier. The goal of the project is not to replace production antivirus engines or secure email gateways, but to provide a transparent, explainable and reproducible research-style tool for phishing triage and cybersecurity portfolio evaluation. The prototype supports English and Greek phishing indicators and includes a Streamlit-based interface for threat scans, dashboard statistics, scan history, evaluation suites and report export. On the final locked evaluation set, Phiraxon AI achieved 87.5% accuracy, 94.1% precision, 80.0% recall and 86.5% F1-score across 40 curated test cases.

title: Development of Structural Diagrams of Digital Infrastructure of Small Modular Reactors
abstract: Digital assets in small modular reactors (SMRs), including instrumentation and control (I&C) systems, plant support systems, and information technologies, are traditionally assessed separately. However, their deployment both improves safety and reliability and introduces new safety and cybersecurity risks. Due to the specific features of SMRs, especially when operating in multi-unit configurations or as part of a grid, digital assets should be considered within an integrated framework referred to as digital infrastructure (DI). This chapter analyzes approaches to assessing the impact of digital systems and technologies on SMR safety and cybersecurity and proposes a formal DI model that includes systems, subsystems, components, and digital technologies connected through geographical, physical, organizational, informational, and logical influences. Several conceptual diagrams of centralized and decentralized SMR control architectures are presented. The goal is to enhance SMR grid safety and reliability through robust digital infrastructure and outline key challenges for DI development.

title: AI-Based Digital Footprint Analyzer
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The rapid growth of internet usage and social media platforms has significantly increased the amount of personal data shared online. Every online activity, including social media interactions, browsing behaviour, comments, uploaded content, and digital transactions, contributes to an individual’s digital footprint. While digital footprints provide convenience and personalization, they also create concerns related to privacy, cybersecurity, identity theft, and online reputation management. Traditional methods of monitoring online presence are often manual, time-consuming, and inefficient in identifying potential security risks. This research paper presents an AI-Based Digital Footprint Analyzer, an intelligent system designed to collect, analyze, and evaluate digital traces generated by users across online platforms. The proposed system utilizes Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques to identify publicly available user information, detect privacy risks, classify sensitive content, and generate security awareness insights. Natural Language Processing (NLP) and data analysis methods are incorporated to examine textual content, behavioural patterns, and exposure levels on digital platforms. The system aims to assist users in understanding their online presence, identifying vulnerable areas, and improving digital privacy management. Experimental analysis demonstrates that AI-driven automation improves the accuracy, efficiency, and scalability of digital footprint assessment compared to traditional monitoring approaches. The study highlights the importance of responsible digital behaviour and demonstrates how AI can contribute to enhanced cybersecurity awareness, privacy protection, and online reputation management. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Digital Footprint, Cybersecurity, Privacy Analysis, Machine Learning, Online Security, NLP, Data Analytics.

title: CLOUD-BASED ACCOUNTING SYSTEMS: EFFICIENCY AND RISK ASSESSMENT
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This article analyzes the role of cloud-based accounting systems in the modern business environment, their advantages over traditional systems, and the risks associated with their implementation. The study examines the impact of cloud technologies on labor productivity and cybersecurity issues. The results indicate that while these systems significantly reduce operational costs, they require a new approach to data security.

title: REAL-TIME FINANCIAL REPORTING IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY: MECHANISMS AND IMPLICATIONS
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Traditional financial reporting is undergoing a radical transformation due to the digital economy. This article explores the mechanisms of Real-Time Financial Reporting (RTFR), focusing on the integration of AI, Cloud Computing, and Blockchain. The research assesses how instantaneous data availability impacts corporate transparency and decision-making. The results suggest that while RTFR significantly reduces information asymmetry and operational delays, it introduces new challenges in cybersecurity and data governance.

title: DeepFake Video Detection Using Hybrid ResNet18-BiLSTM Architecture with Spatiotemporal Learning and Real-Time Forensic Analysis
authors: Faisal Irfan Shaikh; Atharva pisal; Devashish Rajput; Harshad Londhe
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This research presents a hybrid deepfake video detection framework integrating ResNet18 and BiLSTM architectures for robust spatiotemporal forensic analysis. The proposed system combines spatial feature extraction and temporal sequence modeling to detect manipulated videos with high accuracy. Experimental evaluation was conducted using FaceForensics++ and CelebDF datasets. The proposed model achieved 96.30% accuracy and 0.9922 AUC score, demonstrating strong robustness and generalization capability for real-time deepfake detection applications in cybersecurity and multimedia forensics.

title: Specifics of Compliance Risk Management in the Integration of Internet of Things Technologies into Corporate Banking Infrastructure
abstract: The article examines the specific features of compliance risk management in the integration of Internet of Things technologies into corporate banking infrastructure amid deepening digital transformation. The relevance of the study is that the implementation of IoT in the banking environment expands the possibilities for monitoring, control, and operational resilience, while simultaneously creating new regulatory vulnerabilities related to data confidentiality, cybersecurity, transparency in information processing, and dependence on external providers. The purpose of the article is to identify the distinctive characteristics of compliance risk management in a distributed IoT environment and to substantiate approaches to its construction within corporate banking infrastructure. The scientific novelty of the work lies in interpreting compliance risk as an integrative, multilayered category in which technological, legal, operational, and reputational tensions converge. It is concluded that effective management of such risks is possible only within the logic of continuous control throughout the entire life cycle of IoT solutions, including early vulnerability identification, access regulation, logging, monitoring, auditing, vendor assessment, and personnel training. The article will be useful for researchers, banking managers, compliance specialists, information security professionals, and experts in digital transformation.

title: Real Time Phishing Detection Using ML
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: In today’s digital world, phishing attacks have become a major cybersecurity threat. Cybercriminals use fake websites, emails, and links to trick users into sharing sensitive information such as passwords, banking details, and personal data. As online services and remote work continue to grow, phishing attacks are becoming more frequent and advanced. Traditional phishing detection methods mainly depend on blacklists and predefined rules, which are not effective against new or unknown phishing attacks. Manual checking of suspicious links and emails is also slow and difficult. This project, “Real-Time Phishing Detection Using Machine Learning,” aims to develop an intelligent system that can automatically identify phishing websites and emails in real time. The system analyzes features such as URL length, HTTPS usage, suspicious keywords, sender details, and abnormal email behavior. Machine learning algorithms like Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) are trained using phishing and legitimate datasets to improve detection accuracy. Among these models, the Random Forest algorithm gives the best performance because it can handle complex data efficiently and reduce errors. When a phishing attempt is detected, the system immediately alerts the user and provides safety guidance. This project helps improve cybersecurity awareness and provides a smart, scalable, and reliable solution for protecting users from phishing attacks. Humanity built an internet where every second link tries to steal your password. Magnificent achievement, really.

title: Security Frameworks for Operational Technology (OT) and IT Integration
authors: Sudipta Dhar; Shivangi Kashyap; Pravin Kumar
abstract: Today's rapidly evolving industrial environment is witnessing a dramatic change from the accelerated digitization (or digital transformation) of all types of organizations across multiple industries. At the heart of this change is the growing convergence of Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT)—two formerly distinct domains that have traditionally operated with different functions, technologies, and priorities, The convergence of IT and OT represents a new tide of transformation that will drive new technological innovation across the industrial landscape and accelerate automation, efficiency, connectivity, and data. This chapter will consider the potential transformation and challenges associated with the convergence of OT and IT and will also consider the need for common and adaptive approaches to cybersecurity systems.

title: Brainrot: Deskilling and Addiction are Overlooked AI Risks
abstract: The scope of AI safety and alignment work in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has so far mostly been limited to harms related to: (a) discrimination and hate speech, (b) harmful/inappropriate (violent, sexual, illegal) content, (c) information hazards, and (d) use cases related to malicious actors, such as cybersecurity, child abuse, and chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats. The public conversation around AI, on the other hand, has also been focusing on threats to our cognition, mental health, and welfare at large, related to over-relying on new technologies, most recently, those related to GenAI. Examples include deskilling associated with cognitive offloading and the atrophy of critical thinking as a result of over-reliance on GenAI systems, and addiction associated with attachment and dependence on GenAI systems. Such risks are rarely addressed, if at all, in the AI safety and alignment literature. In this paper, we highlight and quantify this discrepancy and discuss some initial thoughts on how safety and alignment work could address cognitive and mental health concerns. Finally, we discuss how information campaigns and regulation can be used to mitigate such prominent risks.

title: Securing Intelligent Healthcare Systems Through Quantum AI and Advanced Cybersecurity
venue: Merging Quantum Cloning and Blockchain Solutions for Health Informatics
abstract: Quantum AI is going to bring the next-generation quantum-proof healthcare systems. High quality health care control systems offer predictive analysis and real time monitoring capability to make intervention in time and with target treatment protocols. The fact that quantum networks can diffuse sequence data makes them more suitable to deal with diffusion of time-series data of the wearable sensor in the real time monitoring of health condition. Further data collection is also facilitated by the incorporation of IoMT devices which result in colossus data on patient health parameters. Management of healthcare processes using quantum frameworks also makes it possible to regulate the processes to achieve peak effectiveness and benefit to the patient.

title: A Post-Quantum-Resilient Iot Device Authentication Cybersecurity Framework Using AI-Driven Anomaly Detection and Blockchain
authors: Abiya Sharon; Sirivella Somanath Vallabhadev; Amirtha Varshini S; Muhammed Shain; Lekshmi B
venue: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering and Management (IRJAEM)
abstract: The rapid increase in the number of Internet of Things (IoT) devices also means that big security issues are coming, especially with the soon-to-be-possible capability of quantum computers to break existing cryptography. Existing methods for authenticating devices in small, low-power IoT networks are too dependent on a central trusted authority, overlook too many unusual and harmful behaviors, and are potentially vulnerable to post-quantum attacks. This paper presents PQ-IoTGuard, a novel hybrid authentication architecture that leverages lattice-based post-quantum cryptography, edge-based lightweight artificial intelligence, and permissioned blockchain to provide quantum-secure, decentralized trust for general IoT networks. By shifting behavioral analysis to edge gateways and employing lattice-based key encapsulation and digital signatures, the framework enables quantum-secure security with only light computational overhead. Experimental assessment carried out in network simulation environments shows that PQ-IoTGuard provides authentication latency of less than 50 milliseconds for networks up to 5,000 devices. It preserves the accuracy of anomaly detection at more than 98% for impersonation attacks and Sybil attacks, and induces a computational overhead of less than 15% compared to traditional PKI systems. Ablation analysis verifies that the combination of post-quantum cryptography, artificial intelligence, and blockchain technology provides synergistic security benefits that cannot be realized by any of these technologies separately. The resilience of the framework against quantum-capable attackers, combined with its scalability and deployability, provides a solid ground for future-proof IoT security infrastructure.

title: A 4-Month Dataset of Interactive SSH Honeypot Logs and Command Payloads [Preprint]
abstract:
This article describes a longitudinal dataset of high-interaction SSH honeypot logs collected over a four-month period from July to November 2025. The data was captured using a custom modular multi-threaded honeypot developed in Python 3.10, utilizing the Paramiko library to simulate an interactive SSHv2 environment. Unlike low-interaction systems, this dataset records the full spectrum of adversary activity, including initial connection attempts, authentication brute-forcing, and post-authentication command execution. The resulting dataset contains 145,425 security events, structured to support session reconstruction via unique identifiers. The telemetry includes source IPv4 addresses, credential pairs, and granular command-line payloads, featuring rare instances of file-less exploitation via bash sockets. This data provides a ground-truth source for training machine learning models for anomaly detection, enhancing SIEM rule-sets, and conducting empirical research into botnet orchestration and manual intrusion tactics in cloud infrastructures.

This is a preprint of a paper submitted to Data in Brief.

This preprint describes the dataset available at DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19815504 and utilizes the software framework archived at DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19817625.

title: Simulation of Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) Using PentesterLab as a Case Study
abstract: This study presents a simulation-based approach to Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) for identifying exploitation techniques in web applications. The research focuses on common web vulnerabilities, including SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), and authentication weaknesses, within a controlled testing environment. Using tools such as Nmap, Metasploit, and automated vulnerability scanners, the study demonstrates how attackers exploit system weaknesses and evaluates corresponding mitigation strategies. The results highlight the effectiveness of combining automated tools with manual testing techniques to improve vulnerability detection and response. This work contributes to enhancing web application security by providing practical insights into exploitation methods and defensive mechanisms against modern cyber threats.

title: REGIONAL INTEGRATION AND ECONOMIC SECURITY
abstract: This study examines the impact of regional economic integration on economic security in Uzbekistan within the context of digital transformation. The research focuses on evaluating the level of economic integration using key indicators such as economic openness, intra-industry trade, and digital integration. The findings reveal that Uzbekistan has experienced a gradual increase in economic openness, reflecting deeper participation in regional and global markets. At the same time, the results indicate that integration processes are uneven across regions, with highly integrated areas contributing more to economic growth but remaining more vulnerable to external shocks. The analysis also shows that digitalization plays a significant role in enhancing integration by improving connectivity and efficiency, while introducing new risks related to cybersecurity and technological dependence. The study highlights the dual nature of integration, emphasizing the need for balanced policies aimed at strengthening economic resilience, reducing regional disparities, and ensuring long-term economic stability in an increasingly interconnected economic environment.

title: A Standards-Aligned IoMT Federated Learning and Blockchain Framework for MITM Mitigation and Risk Quantification using NS-3* [Appendix]
authors: Rajab, Ramadhan Mohamed; Ward, Richard Peter; Abuhmida, Dr Mabrouka; University of South Wales; Romanian-American University; Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers; The Worshipful Livery Company of Wales (WLCoW)
abstract: The increasing reliance on Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) systems introduces critical vulnerabilities to advanced cyber threats such as Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks, which simultaneously compromise data integrity, availability, and clinical safety. This paper presents a standards-aligned security framework integrating a Federated Learning-based Intrusion Detection System (FL-IDS) with blockchain to enable real-time detection, mitigation, and risk quantification of MITM attacks in IoMT networks. The framework is implemented within an NS-3 simulation environment, where MITM attacks are injected and mitigated using distributed, privacy-preserving anomaly detection across heterogeneous devices. Experimental results reveal that MITM attacks produce selective, high-severity disruptions rather than uniform degradation, with critical flow collapse and hybrid anomaly patterns that evade traditional intrusion detection approaches. To quantify attack impact, derived performance metrics—Throughput Reduction Ratio (TRR), Packet Loss Ratio (PLR), Network Delay Increase (NDI), and Jitter Variation Increase (JVI)—are aggregated into a device-weighted Attack Severity Index (wASI). This enables fine-grained, flow-level assessment of clinically relevant degradation. The framework aligns with ISO/IEEE 11073, ISO 14971, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27005, and IEC 80001-1 standards, achieving 94% concordance across clinical, cybersecurity, and governance risk classifications. The proposed approach bridges the gap between fragmented compliance standards by providing a unified, actionable framework for AI-driven intrusion detection, mitigation, and clinically interpretable risk assessment in IoMT environments.

title: RANSOMWARE DETECTION USING MACHINE LEARNING
authors: Rohan Tyagi, Eshan Sharma, Gaurav Yadav, Toshit , Sonika Jalhotra
abstract:
Abstract

Ransomware attacks have emerged as one of the most devastating cybersecurity threats, causing billions of dollars in damage annually and disrupting critical infrastructure worldwide. Traditional signature-based detection methods prove inadequate against evolving ransomware variants that employ sophisticated obfuscation techniques and zero-day exploits. This research presents a comprehensive machine learning-based approach for ransomware detection utilizing static analysis of Portable Executable (PE) file features, addressing the critical need for proactive threat identification without requiring malware execution. The correlation heatmap demonstrated complex inter-feature relationships, with DllCharacteristics emerging as the most discriminative feature for ransomware classification. Feature importance analysis through Random Forest revealed that DllCharacteristics contributed over 20% of the predictive power, followed by DebugRVA, DebugSize, and MajorLinkerVersion, indicating the critical role of PE structural characteristics in malware identification. Three state-of-the-art ensemble learning algorithms were implemented and rigorously evaluated: Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Classifier, and XGBoost. The models utilized a stratified 70-30 train-test split to maintain class balance and ensure generalization capability. Performance evaluation encompassed multiple metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score to provide comprehensive assessment of classification effectiveness. Experimental results demonstrate exceptional performance across all implemented models. Random Forest achieved outstanding results with 99.58% accuracy, 99.69% precision, 99.35% recall, and 99.52% F1-score, establishing it as the top-performing classifier. XGBoost closely followed with 99.55% accuracy, 99.63% precision, 99.32% recall, and 99.48% F1-score. Gradient Boosting Classifier obtained 98.94% accuracy, 99.19% precision, 98.37% recall, and 98.78% F1-score. These results significantly exceed existing benchmarks in ransomware detection literature and demonstrate the efficacy of PE-based feature engineering.

Keywords

Ransomware, machine learning, static analysis, Portable Executable, ensemble learning, Random Forest, XGBoost, cybersecurity.

title: Part 1 AATF v3.1 — Adaptive Adversarial Trace Forensics: Framework Specification
abstract:
AATF v3.1 introduces a unified intelligence‑level intrusion detection framework designed to identify human, scripted, and AI‑assisted adversaries through behavioral geometry, multi‑witness inference, and temporal adaptation metrics. The system models adversarial behavior as a stochastic policy evolving over time and integrates six independent telemetry witnesses—network, authentication, process, filesystem, privilege, and timing—combined through a mutual‑information‑aware fusion model.

 

The framework formalizes signed adaptive behavioral curvature (κ_A), multi‑scale temporal coherence, semantic mutation analysis via the Generative Payload Mutation Index (GPMI), and graph‑based exploration efficiency through the Exploration Compression Ratio (ECR). Additional components include adversarial policy fingerprinting, distributed coordination geometry, a human variability manifold, and an active defense layer that measures adaptive response to controlled perturbations.

 

AATF v3.1 provides a mathematically grounded architecture for real‑time inference in SOC environments, enabling attribution of adversarial intelligence type rather than detection of specific exploits. This paper presents the full theoretical, mathematical, and architectural specification of the framework.

AATF v3.3.1 consolidates and extends the Adversarial Observability Manifold (AOM) Framework into a single, fully integrated technical specification. The framework models adversarial activity not as static signatures, but as trajectories through graph-structured infrastructure state spaces observed under partial visibility. This version introduces the AATF-X Adaptive Observability-Control Architecture, transforming the passive observability engine into an active system capable of dynamic verification, controlled perturbation (including Adaptive Observability Pulses), and adversarial flow shaping. By combining multi-witness inference with behavioral geometry, the framework identifies the nature of the adaptive intelligence generating an attack, rather than focusing solely on payload signatures.

Change Log (v3.3.1 Refinements)

This version incorporates ten substantive refinements over v3.3:

AOM Conceptual Clarification: Explicitly defines the AOM as the detectability structure induced by adversarial behavior, not the behavior itself.

Observability Horizon: Formalizes the absolute limit beyond which adversarial adaptation becomes statistically indistinguishable from stochastic noise.

Curvature Interpretation: Provides tightened guidance to distinguish persistent curvature coherence from stochastic volatility or measurement noise.

Multi-Scale Resonance: Introduces a construct to identify temporal frequencies where adversarial structure is most exposed.

Evasion Strategy Taxonomy: Establishes a formal classification for adaptive adversarial maneuvers.

Identifiability Limitation Clause: Explicitly states that AATF characterizes structural properties and does not assert intent or agency.

Information-Theoretic Interpretation: Frames observability collapse as a degeneration of mutual information.

Reference Implementation Architecture: Provides a standardized blueprint for operational deployment.

Formal Null Hypothesis Statement: Validates system evaluation under adversarial influence.

Versioning Strategy: Codifies the evolution of canonical and operational branches

title: VectraYX-Nano: A 42M-Parameter Spanish Cybersecurity LLM with Native MCP Tool Integration
abstract:
We present VectraYX-Nano, a 41.95M-parameter decoder-only language model trained
from scratch in Spanish for cybersecurity, with a Latin-American regional focus
and native tool invocation via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The model is
built around four contributions. (i) Corpus: VectraYX-Sec-ES, a 170M-token
Spanish corpus assembled by an eight-VM distributed pipeline at ~$25 USD of cloud
compute, partitioned into three curriculum phases: conversational (42M tokens,
OpenSubtitles-ES and OASST1), cybersecurity (118M tokens, NVD, Wikipedia-ES,
in-house Spanish CVE mirror, security blogs), and offensive-security tooling
(10M tokens, ExploitDB, HackTricks, OWASP). (ii) Architecture: a 42M-parameter
Transformer decoder combining Grouped-Query Attention, QK-Norm, RMSNorm, SwiGLU,
RoPE, and a z-loss auxiliary, paired with a domain-balanced 16,384-token
byte-fallback BPE tokenizer. (iii) Curriculum with replay: continual pre-training
across three phases with a replay buffer mitigates catastrophic forgetting and
yields a monotonic loss descent (9.80 -> 3.17 -> 3.00 -> 2.16). After SFT the
released model attains a conversational gate of 0.78 +/- 0.05 over N=4 seeds.
(iv) Two empirical findings: A controlled bootstrap-corpus ablation exposes a
loss-versus-register inversion -- lower-perplexity bootstraps yield worse
conversational behavior at the nano scale. A post-hoc LoRA study shows that the
tool-selection floor of 0.000 on the mixed SFT corpus is a corpus-density
artifact: a tool-dense corpus (2,801 examples, ratio 1:21) raises B4 to
0.145 +/- 0.046 on Nano 42M and 0.445 +/- 0.201 on a 260M mid-tier (N=4 seeds).
The released GGUF artifact is 81 MB in F16 (~20 MB in 4-bit), runs at
sub-second time-to-first-token on commodity hardware, and is, to our knowledge,
the first published Spanish-native cybersecurity LLM with end-to-end MCP
integration.

title: A Comparative Evaluation of Supervised and Reinforcement Learning Techniques for Intrusion Detection in Cybersecurity Systems
authors: Moni Gautam, Gaurav Goel, Preeti Verma
abstract: The high proliferation of networked systems has contributed to high levels of cyberattacks and intrusion detection systems (IDS) has become a key element of the contemporary cybersecurity framework. The classic signature-based IDS methods are not sufficient to counter the developing and the zero-day attacks, and the use of intelligent machine learning techniques is adopted. This paper will provide an in-depth comparative analysis of supervised learning and reinforcement learning methods of intrusion detection in cybersecurity systems. Popular supervised classifiers (Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest (RF), k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Deep Neural Networks (DNN)) are tested in comparison with reinforcement learning models, including Q-Learning and Deep Q-Networks (DQN), on a benchmark intrusion detection dataset. The experimental findings support the idea that the application of supervised learning models has the high performance in terms of detection in the stationary environment with Random Forest and DNN giving the performance at 96.8 and 97.5 percent, respectively, and F1-score of over 0.96. They however perform poorly when subjected to new patterns of attack. Conversely, reinforcement learning models are more adaptable with the DQN-based IDS showing 94.2 detection accuracy, false positive rate of 3.1, and stability in detecting attacks over time in dynamic attack environments. Even though reinforcement learning models take more time to train, they are more resilient to emerging threats. The comparative analysis reveals the trade-offs between accuracy and adaptability and provides an idea that hybrid IDS frameworks combining supervised and reinforcement learning methods can provide better cybersecurity resilience.

title: AN ADAPTIVE FOCAL LOSS-BASED XGBOOST FRAMEWORK WITH SELECTIVE BLOCKCHAIN LOGGING FOR SECURE INTRUSION DETECTION IN IoT FARM NETWORKS
abstract:
Internet of Things (IoT) technologies in smart agriculture have enhanced monitoring,
automation, and decision-making, but also present major security challenges, including DDoS,
spoofing, and data injection attacks. Such threats are especially hard to identify because the
data related to the IoT networks is highly imbalanced, with instances of attacks being
underrepresented. In dealing with this, the paper suggests an Adaptive Focal Loss-based
Extreme Gradient Boosting (AFL-XGB) framework to the efficient intrusion detection in IoTbased farm setups. The model uses a dynamically scaled focal loss term that maximizes
minority attack detection and minimizes false negatives, increasing generalization as compared
to traditional methods. Further, selective blockchain record mechanism is proposed where only
high-confidence benign information is stored, which reduces storage overhead and maintains
data integrity and trust to distributed systems. Experimental results through the Farm-Flow
dataset illustrate that the proposed model is able to achieve a higher performance, with 96%
accuracy, 94.5% F1-score, and 0.97 AUC in comparison to the traditional models of SVM,
Random Forest, and the default XGBoost. Another advantage of the framework is that it
minimizes the blockchain storage overhead. Altogether, the proposed AFL-XGB system offers
a scalable, secure and efficient intrusion detection solution to smart agriculture IoT systems.

title: The Digital Divide as a Global Security Challenge: Assessing Governance Mechanisms
abstract: The digital divide has evolved from a developmental concern into a critical global security challenge shaping economic stability, political governance, and cybersecurity resilience. While access to digital technologies has expanded globally, significant disparities persist between and within states, particularly between developed and developing regions. These inequalities undermine global security governance by weakening cyber capacity, increasing exposure to cyber threats, and limiting participation in digital governance systems. This study adopts a qualitative empirical approach, drawing on secondary data from international institutions such as the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), World Bank, and United Nations reports. It argues that the digital divide is no longer solely an issue of access but a structural security vulnerability embedded in global governance systems. Findings reveal that unequal ICT infrastructure, weak cyber capacity in developing states, and fragmented international regulatory frameworks contribute to global insecurity. The paper concludes that effective governance mechanisms must shift from access-oriented policies to capacity-building, cyber resilience, and inclusive digital governance frameworks.

title: Corruption Reduction in Bangladesh by Introducing Modern FinTech: Opportunities, Challenges, and Policy Framework
abstract:
Corruption remains one of the major barriers to sustainable economic development in Bangladesh.
Traditional cash-based transactions, weak institutional monitoring, financial exclusion, bureaucratic
inefficiency, and political interference have intensified bribery, money laundering, tax evasion, and
financial fraud. Modern Financial Technology (FinTech) provides a transformative opportunity to
reduce corruption through digital payments, blockchain systems, artificial intelligence (AI), biometric
verification, regulatory technology (RegTech), and transparent financial ecosystems. This paper
investigates how FinTech can reduce corruption in Bangladesh by improving transparency,
accountability, transaction traceability, and financial inclusion. The study adopts a qualitative
analytical approach supplemented by quantitative secondary data drawn from policy reports,
academic literature, Bangladesh Bank publications, Transparency International datasets, and recent
financial-crime investigations. Findings indicate that Mobile Financial Services (MFS), digital banking,
e-governance platforms, blockchain-enabled public procurement, and AI-driven Anti-Money
Laundering (AML) systems can significantly reduce informal cash transactions and administrative
corruption. However, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, regulatory weaknesses, political influence, and
digital inequality remain substantial challenges. The paper proposes a comprehensive policy
framework integrating central-bank oversight, digital identity systems, blockchain governance,
AI-powered fraud detection, and financial-literacy initiatives.
Keywords: FinTech, Corruption Reduction, Digital Payments, Blockchain, Bangladesh, Mobile Financial
Services, Financial Transparency, AI Governance, E-Governance, Digital Banking

title: Neural Sentinel: Automated Security Auditing for LLM, RAG, and Agentic Systems Under the EU AI Act
abstract:
The EU AI Act (Article 15) mandates robustness and cybersecurity for high‑risk AI systems. Small and medium‑sized enterprises
(SMEs) using Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG), or agentic workflows lack affordable tools
to assess compliance. This paper introduces Neural Sentinel, a suite of five gRPC‑based security scanners that automate the detection
of critical vulnerabilities: prompt injection, system prompt leakage, data exfiltration, document poisoning, tool hijacking, memory
poisoning, and post‑quantum cryptography weaknesses.
Unlike open‑source scanners (Garak, Counterfit), Neural Sentinel produces a 1‑page compliance report mapped directly to the EU AI
Act. Unlike commercial scanners (Lakera, ProtectAI), it offers a free, asynchronous audit model requiring only the client’s system
prompt – no API key, no integration. Attack taxonomies (RAG01‑07, AGT01‑08) are documented, and eight public demo videos
demonstrate real critical findings. The scanners are live on the SingularityNET mainnet (Ethereum) and have been tested against
100+ synthetic prompts, achieving an 86% detection rate for known injection patterns. This paper demonstrates that low‑cost,
automated, compliance‑oriented security audits are feasible and can help Italian SMEs meet the August 2026 EU AI Act deadline.

title: AI-Powered Web Application Firewall for Intelligent Threat Detection and Prevention
authors: DEVAK BIN; AARNA AGGARWAL; Dr. R Deebalakshmi
abstract:
This paper presents the design and implementation of an AI-powered Web Application Firewall (WAF) aimed at enhancing web security through intelligent threat detection. Traditional WAFs rely on static rule-based systems, which are often ineffective against evolving cyber threats such as zero-day attacks and sophisticated injection techniques.

The proposed system integrates machine learning algorithms to dynamically analyze incoming web traffic and identify malicious patterns in real time. By leveraging anomaly detection and pattern recognition techniques, the system can detect SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), and other application-layer attacks with improved accuracy.

The solution is designed to continuously learn from new data, thereby improving its detection capabilities over time. Experimental results demonstrate that the AI-based WAF outperforms traditional approaches in terms of detection rate and adaptability, making it a robust solution for modern web security challenges.

title: Leveraging artificial intelligence for enhanced disaster response coordination
abstract: This review critically examines the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in coordinating the core phases of disaster response: preparedness, response, recovery, and mitigation.  Drawing on illustrative case studies such as AI-driven flood forecasting with Delft-FEWS, post-disaster damage mapping via DroneDeploy, and optimised emergency dispatch through RescueME. It synthesises evidence on five core AI capabilities (machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, natural language processing, and optimisation algorithms). We find that AI can substantially improve predictive accuracy, real-time situational awareness, rapid decision-making, resource allocation, and inter-agency collaboration, thereby addressing the speed and complexity challenges of traditional disaster management. However, adoption is hindered by fragmented data ecosystems, opaque “black box” models, interoperability gaps, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, ethical and equity concerns, and limited accessibility in low-resource settings. To overcome these barriers, we argue for the development of interoperable data standards, explainable AI frameworks, robust cyber governance protocols, and inclusive stakeholder engagement. Emerging trends, such as the convergence of AI with IoT and edge computing, enhanced human-AI decision support, and the democratisation of AI tools, offer promising pathways for building more resilient, scalable, and ethically grounded disaster response systems. By aligning technological innovation with human oversight and participatory governance, strategic integration of AI can enhance preparedness, response effectiveness, and recovery efficiency, fostering safer and more resilient communities worldwide.

title: Implications of artificial intelligence and cyberspace on risk management capabilities
authors: Beriša, Hatidža; Cvetković, Vanja; Pavić, Aleksandar
abstract: The crisis management system is a key element of a modern, reliable, effective, and sustainable security system. In contemporary settings, management functions are implemented through the capabilities of a command-information system. Consequently, most activities are conducted within cyberspace, meaning that management functions cannot be effectively executed without adequate telecommunications and information technology support. The primary target of hostile cyber activities is precisely the command-information system. Developing an optimal methodology for the use of command-information systems, as well as for prevention and protection against cyber-attacks, is among the most critical tasks for modern defence and security systems. One approach to enhancing risk management is through the application of artificial intelligence (AI). AI should ensure superiority in cyberspace, primarily at the national level, providing the foundation for executing legitimate and lawful cyber activities in a state's defence system. This paper aims to explore the role and significance of artificial intelligence within the realm of cybersecurity by analyzing its implications for risk management in contemporary environments. Command in modern military operations, the nature of modern warfare risks, the protection of command-information systems, the autonomy of artificial intelligence in decision-making, and an understanding of cyber threats are factors through which the challenges of modern command systems can be understood.

title: Ethical and Privacy Concerns of AI Chatbots in Customer Relationship Management
abstract:
This research article examines the ethical and privacy concerns associated with the use of AI-powered chatbots in Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems. As organizations increasingly adopt Artificial Intelligence technologies to automate customer interactions, personalize communication, and improve service efficiency, concerns regarding data privacy, transparency, fairness, and ethical AI usage have become increasingly important in modern digital business environments.

The study explores how AI chatbots collect, process, and analyze large volumes of customer data to support personalized marketing, customer engagement, and automated service delivery. While these technologies improve operational efficiency and customer responsiveness, they also raise concerns related to unauthorized data access, surveillance, algorithmic bias, misinformation, lack of transparency, and customer trust in automated systems.

The article analyzes the ethical implications of AI-driven customer interactions, including issues surrounding informed consent, accountability, explainability, emotional manipulation, and the replacement of human communication with automated systems. It also examines privacy regulations, AI governance frameworks, cybersecurity risks, and responsible AI practices aimed at protecting customer rights and maintaining trust in digital relationship management systems.

In addition, the study highlights emerging opportunities for developing transparent, secure, and customer-centered AI chatbot systems that balance innovation with ethical responsibility. This work contributes to ongoing discussions on responsible AI adoption and emphasizes the importance of ethical governance and data protection in the future of AI-driven customer relationship management.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Crime: Challenges of Criminal Liability in the Age of Algorithms
authors: Hamouti, Nadia; El Bakouhi Safae, Safae
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly playing a vital role in the criminal law domain, both as a means to prevent and fight criminal offenses and as a means that gives rise to new forms of criminal offenses. Therefore, the main objective of this article is to analyse the role of artificial intelligence in the prevention and fight against criminal offenses, as well as the challenges it poses to criminal law at the national and international levels. In this context, it is necessary to refer to the role of artificial intelligence in surveillance, criminal investigation, cybersecurity, and criminal justice, while focusing on the risks associated with its use for criminal purposes. Regarding the methodology used in this research paper, it is necessary to refer to the fact that it is based on an analytical and critical approach to the subject matter, focusing on the study of legislative frameworks at the national and international levels, as well as reports and cases related to cybercrime. This methodology enables the evaluation of the sufficiency of the criminal law rules in the context of the criminal offenses related to artificial intelligence, in particular concerning criminal liability and the protection of fundamental freedoms. This article shows that, in spite of the opportunities offered by AI to improve the efficiency of the criminal justice system, the lack of a harmonized legal framework generates legal uncertainty. It highlights the need to adapt criminal law in order to ensure the effective prosecution of AI-related crimes while guaranteeing the fundamental principles of legality, proportionality, and the protection of human rights.

title: PhishAlert: A Risk-Based URL Detection System for Identifying Phishing Websites
authors: Sangeetha M, Raja Sherina T, Mrs.J.Doulas
abstract: Phishing attacks constitute a serious cybersecurity issue where users are lured into entering false URLs to acquire critical data such as passwords and bank details. Users often face difficulty determining whether the URL is a legitimate one or not. PhishAlert A Risk Based URL Detection System attempts to solve the above problem by offering an efficient solution. It is a web application that assesses the URLs and classifies them into safe, suspicious, or phishing. The system employs a rule-based algorithm that examines different attributes of the URL, such as the utilisation of the HTTPS protocol, suspicious terms such as 'login', 'verify', and 'bank', the length of the URL, special characters, and multiple sub-domains. Depending upon the attributes, a risk score is computed, and a classification is made. The program also provides the reasons behind the classification to increase the awareness of the users. It incorporates VirusTotal for verifying the URLs through several security engines. It has a dashboard and history section as well. In addition, the software is developed in such a way that even those who do not have technical skills can examine the security of any URL without much effort. The dashboard displays the scan report in charts, making it easier for users to know how many URLs are safe, suspicious, or phishing. The history section retains all URLs that have been checked before, allowing the user to examine, filter, and download their information whenever necessary. The system uses both the rules method and outside sources to ensure more reliable results

title: Gap Between Cybercrime Awareness and Preventive Practices - A Survey-Based Study
authors: Diwakar Neopaney; Parikshit Vyas; Gunjan Mundra
abstract: People use the internet for everything nowadays including communication, online shopping, and money transfers. This has made people's lives very easy but it can make people vulnerable to cybercrimes. So, it is important for people to know how to stay safe online. Even though different programs make people aware of cybercrimes, they do not follow proper precautions. The result shows that 96.17% people are aware of the risk like using public wi-fi for payment transactions, reusing the same password everywhere and clicking on unknown links yet they put themselves on risk and fall victims to cybercrimes the result shows the main reason for the gap are carelessness, lack of knowledge, time constrain. The research concludes that both awareness and behavior need improvement.

Week 2: TVC verification and escalation — cross-domain structural correspondences verified for Tarski independence. Mathematical and logical canonicals locked. Coding and cybersecurity profile clusters formed.
Week 2–3: Canonical formation and fine-tuning — confirmed canonicals injected into training signal. Deductive reasoning chains reinforced. Model evaluated against target benchmarks and iterated.

Conflict register item C-005 (active): The "Claude Mythos" framing in the paper assumes Mythos's performance gains are primarily attributable to PACAD-based training.
